text: The Crucible was a primordial convergence of all living things, described in item descriptions as the source from which all life in the Lands Between originally came.
In the age of the Crucible, life was not divided into species or hierarchies but existed in chaotic communion, with traits like tails, wings, and carapaces expressing freely.
An older tree called the Great Tree existed at the center of the Crucible age, predating the current Erdtree, referenced in items like the Root Resin and the Crucible Knight armor set.
Ancient dragons existed before the Golden Order and may have had their own prior cosmic order and god predating the Greater Will.
The Golden Order reached an accommodation with some ancient dragons rather than conquering all of them outright, as evidenced by dragon communion rituals involving consuming dragon hearts.
A distant cosmic presence called the Greater Will sent a daughter, Marika, and a golden being called the Elden Beast toward the Lands Between.
The current Erdtree grew around the Elden Ring, absorbing and subsuming the older Great Tree that existed before it.
An incantation description states that everything was originally in opposition to the tree, but through countless victories in war it became the embodiment of order.
Murals from the Golden Order's early era, called the Age of Plenty, depict the Erdtree standing straight and tall, unlike its leaning posture in the game's present.
Traces of the Rune of Death spread through the Erdtree's root network, appearing as Death Root.
The spread of the Rune of Death created a new category of beings called 'those who live in death,' undead people who cannot properly return to the Erdtree.
Every demigod touched by a Great Rune's concentrated power was driven toward madness.
The Erdtree in the game's present cannot be entered, its golden bark sealed over by thorns that no conventional weapon can break.
Sorcerers claim the Erdtree is withered while priests claim it is merely dormant awaiting a new Elden Lord.
The Realm of Shadow contains the Gate of Divinity, the same gate Marika used to become a god.
The game identifies at least half a dozen Outer Gods clearly, with hints of others whose names remain obscure.
The God of Scarlet Rot is an ancient deity that was defeated and sealed beneath the lakes, in what became the Lake of Rot.
The Formless Mother, also called the Mother of Truth, is the Outer God that Mohg worships, associated with burning blood, wounds, and brutal intimacy.
The Fell God is depicted as a malformed one-eyed deity with curled horns and braided red hair, associated with primordial fire preceding the Erdtree's golden warmth.
The Frenzied Flame is delivered through the Three Fingers, said to be a counterpart to the Greater Will's Two Fingers, once part of a single whole.
The Dark Moon, Ranni's chosen Outer God, is cold, silver, and distant, governing fate, stars, and the unknown, offering freedom rather than commandment.
The player character is called Tarnished, one who once had the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, was exiled, died, and is now called back by a new Grace to seek the Elden Lordship.
The ruins of Limgrave suggest a civilization that was once whole.
The Academy of Raya Lucaria represents a tradition of magical scholarship that persisted stubbornly even as the world fell apart.
The Mountaintops of the Giants reflect a genocide carried out in the name of order.
The Tarnished's journey leads through demigods, ruins, underground cities, and frozen mountaintops before reaching Leyndell, the royal capital.
The Lands Between is ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal, and the Elden Ring is the source of the Erdtree.
Demigods are described as warped Lords who began as members of a royal and noble family, ruling their domains with power granted by shards of the Elden Ring.
Those blessed by the Elden Ring and Erdtree are marked by a golden aura visible in their eyes.
The Lands Between is divided into seven distinct areas: Limgrave, Caelid, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Mt. Gelmir, Mountaintops of the Giants, and underground river locations.
Each of the seven areas of the Lands Between is overseen by a Demigod.
If an Empyrean defies the will of the Two Fingers, their Shadow is fated to go mad and oppose them.
Before the Erdtree, the horns of an Omen signified divinity, but after the Golden Order's establishment, Omens were seen as cursed beings without grace, having their horns cut off and being enslaved.
The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC takes players to the Realm of Shadow, a dark, death-filled counterpart of the Lands Between hidden beneath a shrouded cloud south of the Erdtree.
The Realm of Shadow features the Scadutree, a shadowy counterpart to the Erdtree.
The DLC's story centers on the ambitions of Miquella, Messmer, and St. Trina, and explores the history of the Hornsent faction.
